status.note: The panel half of the Tabs pair. It is a member of the SAME collection as TabItem, which collection.items — a single component name — cannot express.

intent.purpose: The content one tab reveals. It exists so the strip has something real to control: a tab announcing that it opens a panel, with no panel wired to it, describes an interaction that does not happen.
behaviour: Matches its value against the selection on the surrounding Tabs and hides itself when it does not match.
Stays in the document while hidden, so scroll position and anything a consumer measured survive switching away and back.
Is focusable in its own right, so a keyboard user leaving the strip has somewhere to land even when the panel holds nothing focusable.
Names itself from its tab, so it is announced with the tab's label rather than needing its own.
Throws if rendered outside a Tabs.
notFor: Content that should unmount when hidden. This panel stays in the document by design.
Lazy loading. Nothing here defers rendering, and selection follows focus, so arrowing across the strip renders every panel in turn.
Use without a TabItem of the same value — the panel would have no accessible name and no way to be shown.

selected.description: Derived from the surrounding Tabs by comparing value.
selected.visual: The panel is shown; otherwise it is hidden.

a11y.keyboard: Reachable with Tab immediately after the chosen tab. It shows no focus ring of its own.
notes: The accessible name comes entirely from the matching tab. If no tab carries the same value, the panel is announced unnamed and nothing detects that pairing.

It is focusable unconditionally, which is the practice for a panel that may hold nothing focusable. The cost is a Tab stop on every panel, including ones full of focusable content that did not need it.
It takes no focus ring, so a keyboard user landing on it gets no visible confirmation. That is the common convention and still a real gap.

children.description: Anything. The panel makes no assumptions about its content.

root.description: The panel region. Its only paint is the space separating it from the strip.
